properties.name: Epic of Gilgamesh
properties.summary: King Gilgamesh of Uruk, two-thirds god, befriended the wild man Enkidu. Together they slew Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven. When Enkidu died, Gilgamesh sought immortality from flood-survivor Utnapishtim. He found the plant of youth but a serpent stole it. He returned home accepting mortality, his legacy being the walls of Uruk.

properties.name: Enuma Elish — Babylonian Creation
properties.summary: From the mixing of sweet water (Apsu) and salt water (Tiamat) came the first gods. When Apsu plotted to destroy them, Enki killed him. Tiamat raised an army of monsters. Marduk slew Tiamat, splitting her body to form heaven and earth. Humans were created from Kingu's blood to serve the gods.

properties.name: Ishtar's Descent to the Underworld
properties.summary: Ishtar descended through the seven gates of the underworld, removing one garment at each gate until she stood naked before her sister Ereshkigal, queen of the dead. The world above withered without her. She was rescued but had to send a substitute — her lover Tammuz, who would spend half the year below.

properties.name: The Great Flood (Utnapishtim)
properties.summary: The gods decided to destroy humanity with a flood. Enki warned Utnapishtim, who built a great boat and loaded it with animals and craftsmen. After seven days the flood subsided. Utnapishtim released a dove, swallow, and raven. The gods granted him immortality. This predates the biblical Noah story.

properties.name: Etana — The King Who Flew to Heaven
properties.summary: King Etana of Kish had no heir. An eagle, punished for betraying a serpent, was rescued by Etana in exchange for carrying him to heaven to find the Plant of Birth. Riding the eagle ever higher, Etana looked down and the earth shrank to nothing. Whether he succeeded remains unknown — the tablet is broken.

properties.name: Adapa and Immortality Lost
properties.summary: Adapa, a wise priest of Enki, broke the wing of the South Wind. Summoned before Anu in heaven, Enki warned him not to eat or drink anything offered. Anu, impressed by Adapa's wisdom, offered the food and water of immortality. Following Enki's advice, Adapa refused — and humanity lost its chance at eternal life.
